content.title: WWE WrestleMania 42 Sunday: What Time Does It Start Tonight?
content.text: Start time, full card, and how to watch WrestleMania 42 Sunday night.Apr 19, 2026 4:18 PM EDTJohn Cena stands in the ring during WrestleMania 42 at Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas as host.Getty Images Update: WWE announced during the WrestleMania Countdown show a change to tonight’s card. Raw General Manager Adam Pearce confirmed that Dominik Mysterio will now face “The Demon” Finn Bálor in a Street Fight. WrestleMania 42 continues tonight at 6 p.m. ET (5 p.m. CT / 3 p.m. PT). The event will stream live on ESPN Unlimited in the United States and on Netflix internationally. Fans can also catch the first hour on ESPN via traditional cable and live TV streaming platforms. As you get ready for the show, here’s a quick recap of Night One and a look at tonight’s full card. John Cena will return to host Night Two of WrestleMania 42.Getty Images What Happened During Night One? WrestleMania Saturday delivered several major moments, highlighted by the return of Paige, who came back nearly a decade after a career-ending neck injury and won the WWE Women’s Tag Team Championships alongside Brie Bella. Watch highlights from WrestleMania 42 Night One below: Bron Breakker also returned from injury, with a viral moment showing him sprinting down the entrance ramp. Bianca Belair made headlines as well, announcing her pregnancy in front of the WrestleMania crowd. For a full recap, read the complete WrestleMania 42 Night One results here. What Is Tonight’s Card? On paper, Sunday’s card is stacked, with two of the weekend’s biggest matches set to open and close the show. Brock Lesnar vs. Oba Femi will open WrestleMania 42 Sunday.Getty Images World Heavyweight Championship: CM Punk (c) vs. Roman ReignsWWE Women’s Championship: Jade Cargill (c) vs. Rhea RipleyUnited States Championship: Sami Zayn (c) vs. Trick WilliamsStreet Fight: “The Demon” Finn Bálor vs. Dominik MysterioIntercontinental Championship — Ladder Match: Penta vs. Rey Mysterio vs. Je’Von Evans vs. Dragon Lee vs. Rusev vs. JD McDonaghSingles Match: Brock Lesnar vs. Oba Femi How Long Is WrestleMania? Night One ran approximately 3.5 hours. Night Two is expected to run a similar length, putting the projected end time between 9:30–10 p.m. ET (8:30–9 p.m. CT / 6:30–7 p.m. PT). A post-show will immediately follow on ESPN Unlimited, as well as on WWE’s YouTube channel.
